h1: The Oldest Football Competition in the World
lead: Every tournament in the world traces back to one: the FA Cup, created in 1871. Here is the story of football's oldest competition — and the trophies and leagues that followed it.
thumbCaption: The oldest football competition in the world
share: The FA Cup is the world's oldest football competition. Here is the story of the cup that started it all.
content:
Before there were Champions Leagues, World Cups or domestic super leagues, there was a simple idea: gather a group of clubs, knock them out over several rounds, and give a trophy to the last one standing. That idea was born in England in 1871, and the competition it created — the FA Cup — has never stopped running since.

The FA Cup: The First Ever

The Football Association launched its cup competition in the 1871-72 season, just eight years after the FA itself was founded. Fifteen clubs entered. The final was played at Kennington Oval in London, where the Wanderers — a team of former public-school players — beat the Royal Engineers 1-0. The only goal of the match was scored by Morton Betts, playing under the pseudonym 'A.H. Chequer'.

That first trophy, known as the 'little tin idol', was 45 centimetres tall, cost around £20, and was stolen from a Birmingham shop window in 1895 and never recovered. The FA Cup that is lifted today is a modern replica of its 1911 replacement, but the competition itself has run continuously for more than 150 years — the oldest national football competition in the world.

The Trophy That Predates It: The Youdan Cup

Strictly speaking, a trophy was awarded for football earlier. The Youdan Cup was contested in 1867 in Sheffield and is considered the first trophy ever played for in football history. But it was played under the Sheffield rules, a separate code of football that predated the FA's Laws of the Game, so it is not counted as an 'association football' competition. That honour belongs to the FA Cup.

The Oldest Trophy: The Scottish Cup

If you measure by the trophy itself rather than the competition, the answer changes. The Scottish Cup was first contested in 1873-74, and the original trophy — a silver vase — is the oldest association football trophy in existence, having been presented to the winners in 1874. Scotland's competition is therefore the second-oldest national cup and the holder of the oldest surviving piece of silverware.

The World's First League: The Football League

A cup is one thing; a league is another. The world's first football league was founded on 17 April 1888 at the Royal Hotel in Manchester, the brainchild of Aston Villa director William McGregor. Twelve clubs from the Midlands and the north of England signed up, and the first season began on 8 September 1888.

Preston North End won that inaugural title without losing a single match — earning the nickname 'The Invincibles' — and went on to complete the first-ever League and FA Cup double in 1888-89. The Football League's founding is why England is credited with creating not just the game's rules but its structure: every professional league in the world is a descendant of that 1888 format.

The Oldest International-Style Cups

Other countries followed quickly. The Copa del Rey, Spain's national cup, was founded in 1903 and is among the oldest national competitions outside Britain, with Athletic Bilbao its first winners. The Copa America began in 1916, and the World Cup itself arrived in 1930 in Uruguay — all of them descendants of the template the FA Cup set in 1871.

FA Cup (England)1871Oldest national football competition
Scottish Cup1873Oldest surviving football trophy
Football League (England)1888World's first football league
Copa del Rey (Spain)1903One of the oldest national cups
Copa America1916Oldest continental international competition
The bottom line: The FA Cup is football's oldest competition, the Scottish Cup its oldest trophy, and the Football League the ancestor of every league on Earth. England gave football its rules — and its very sense of competitive structure.

h1: The Largest Football Stadiums in the World
lead: Football's biggest grounds hold more people than many towns. From a 114,000-seat colossus in North Korea to the cathedrals of Europe, here are the largest football stadiums in the world.
thumbCaption: The largest football stadiums in the world
share: 114,000 seats in Pyongyang, 99,354 at Camp Nou. The world's largest football stadiums, ranked by capacity.
content:
Stadiums are football's cathedrals, and a few of them are genuinely colossal. The biggest grounds in the world are measured in the tens of thousands of seats — and one in North Korea holds more spectators than any stadium on Earth has ever held for football.

The World's Largest: Rungrado 1st of May Stadium

The largest football stadium in the world is the Rungrado 1st of May Stadium in Pyongyang, North Korea, with an official capacity of 114,000. Opened in 1989, its huge scalloped roof is shaped like magnolia petals, and it is best known for hosting the Arirang mass games rather than regular club football. It is the only stadium on Earth where the crowd alone could fill a small city.

The Great Cathedrals of the Modern Game

After Rungrado, the list of genuinely massive football stadiums is dominated by national stadiums, tournament venues and a few legendary club homes.

Camp Nou: The Biggest Club Stadium

Europe's largest stadium is Barcelona's Camp Nou, which holds 99,354 people and is the biggest club-owned football ground in the world. It has been the scene of more than 60 years of the club's most famous nights. The stadium is currently undergoing a major renovation as Barcelona prepare for the 2030 World Cup, with the rebuilt capacity expected to reach around 105,000 — which would put it within touching distance of Rungrado.

Wembley: The Home of English Football

London's Wembley Stadium is the largest in England, seating 90,000 beneath its iconic arch. It is the spiritual home of the England national team and has hosted the final of the 1966 World Cup, the 2012 Olympic football and the European Championship, including the dramatic Euro 2020 final. Its 90,000 seats make it one of the ten biggest football stadiums anywhere.

The 2026 World Cup Factor

The 2026 World Cup, co-hosted by the United States, Mexico and Canada, brought a new set of giant venues into the football spotlight. The final was played at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey — an 82,500-seat stadium that became the biggest World Cup final venue in history. Estadio Azteca in Mexico City achieved its own piece of history by becoming the first stadium to host World Cup matches in three different editions (1970, 1986 and 2026).

Why Bigger Isn't Always Better

Capacity is a matter of pride, but the biggest stadiums are rarely the most atmospheric. Clubs like Barcelona and Juventus have discussed or built smaller, more intimate grounds in recent years because a full 40,000-seat bowl generates more noise than a half-empty 90,000-seat one. The loudest football crowds in history, after all, have come from stadiums far smaller than Rungrado.

Quick answer: The largest football stadium in the world is Rungrado 1st of May Stadium (114,000). The largest club stadium is Camp Nou (99,354). The biggest World Cup final venue ever was MetLife Stadium (82,500) in 2026.
